# Awesome Design Language System — External Reference Index

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/DragorWW/awesome-design-language-system
- Maintainer: DragorWW
- License: MIT
- Source type: curated external reference index
- Scope: digital design systems, design-language frameworks, visual-language systems, style guides, grids, frontend design-system libraries, tooling, and related articles

## Why this belongs in the knowledge base

This repository is useful as a discovery and benchmarking source for the Prompt-library workflow. It collects established design systems and practical resources that can support research, visual-system analysis, style-system development, art direction, and quality-control stages.

It should be treated as an external reference index rather than as an authoritative project rule. Individual references discovered through this source should be evaluated independently before being promoted into project-specific or system-level rules.

## Main knowledge categories

### 1. Design-system construction

Resources concerning how to build and structure design systems, including component standardization, proportional scales, and Atomic Design.

Potential workflow use:
- research framing
- system decomposition
- component taxonomy
- reusable design primitives

### 2. Established design-language systems

Examples include major public design systems and brand/style systems such as:
- Atlassian Design Language
- BBC GEL
- IBM Carbon
- Google Material Design
- Apple Human Interface Guidelines
- Microsoft Design
- Shopify Polaris
- GitLab Pajamas
- Salesforce Lightning Design System
- other institutional and commercial design systems

Potential workflow use:
- reference research
- comparative analysis
- visual-system benchmarking
- hierarchy and consistency studies

### 3. Frontend design-system libraries

The source indexes implementation-oriented systems and component libraries such as React-, Vue-, and multi-framework UI systems.

Potential workflow use:
- translating visual systems into reusable component logic
- understanding design-token and component relationships
- evaluating scalability between design and implementation

### 4. Design-system tools

Examples indexed by the source include:

Potential workflow use:

## Suggested consumers in Prompt-library

Primary:
- RES-001 — visual/reference research
- RES-002 — reference selection and evaluation
- VIS-001 — composition analysis
- VIS-005 — typography analysis
- VDNA-001 — visual-DNA synthesis
- ART-001 / ART-002 / ART-003 — art-direction development
- QC-001 / QC-002 / QC-003 — consistency and system-quality checks

Secondary:
- GEN-001 / GEN-002 when a project explicitly requires modular or design-system-aware generation

## Retrieval guidance

Use this source when the task involves concepts such as:

- design system
- design language
- visual language
- style guide
- component system
- design tokens
- grid system
- spacing system
- vertical rhythm
- UI pattern library
- reusable visual components
- design-system documentation

Do not automatically import stylistic decisions from any linked design system. First identify the relevant principle, compare it against the current project brief and visual DNA, and classify the result as reference evidence, transferable principle, or project-specific rule.

## Provenance note

This knowledge file summarizes and indexes the external repository for discovery purposes. The original repository remains the source of provenance for its links and categorization.
